You are fixing a bug in the Python dateutil repository checked out at /dateutil (do NOT look at any other copy of dateutil on the system, do not use the internet). Work only inside /dateutil.

GOAL: Fix the bug in /dateutil/dateutil/rrule.py that makes `rrule(DAILY, count=0, dtstart=datetime(1997,9,2,9,0))` behave as if no count were given (it currently yields occurrences all the way to year 9999 instead of yielding nothing). The hidden test is `dateutil.test.test_rrule.RRuleTest::testCountZero`; its expected behaviour is that a count of 0 means zero occurrences: `list(rrule(DAILY, count=0, dtstart=...)) == []`, `rrule(DAILY, count=0, ...).count() == 0`, and `list(rrulestr("FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=0", dtstart=...)) == []`. Also `str()` of such a rule should still round-trip through `rrulestr`.

WHERE: In `rrule._iter` there are two places using `if count:` / `if not count:` (around lines 849-851 and 866-868 of dateutil/rrule.py), and `rrule.__str__` uses `if self._count:` (around line 692). `count=None` must keep meaning "unbounded".

CONSTRAINTS: Make the minimal change. Do NOT edit or delete any test file. Do NOT break any currently passing test. Run `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test/ -q` before and after your change and make sure the set of failures does not grow (report the before/after failure lists).

REPORT: state exactly which lines you changed, the new code, and the pytest results before/after.

You are fixing bugs in the Python dateutil repository checked out at /dateutil (do NOT look at any other copy of dateutil on the system, do not use the internet). Work only inside /dateutil.

GOAL: Fix TWO bugs in /dateutil/dateutil/parser.py.

BUG A (hidden test `dateutil.test.test_parser.ParserTest::testFuzzyWithTokens`): the fuzzy_with_tokens behaviour of `parser.parse` is wrong. The repository's own visible test testFuzzyWithTokens currently passes, so the hidden version of the test uses different input; the expected behaviour is that with `fuzzy_with_tokens=True`, `parse` returns `(datetime, tuple_of_skipped_tokens)` where the skipped tokens are the pieces of the input string that were not used, in order, with consecutive skipped tokens recombined into one string (see the `skipped_tokens` / `last_skipped_token_i` logic around lines 679-680 and 1030-1042 of dateutil/parser.py). Find the injected defect in that logic (compare carefully how `last_skipped_token_i` is initialised/updated and how tokens are recombined) and fix it minimally. Also check the `_parse` return path at line ~1062 and the `parse()` return path at line ~612.

BUG B (hidden test `dateutil.test.test_parser.ParserTest::test_idx_check`): there is an injected index/bounds defect in `_parse` in dateutil/parser.py - some `l[i]` / `l[i+1]` / `l[i+2]` / `l[i+3]` access is missing a bounds check (or a bounds check was changed), which can raise IndexError or misparse near the end of the token list. Find it and fix it minimally. Note the test name is `test_idx_check`, which in the upstream project checks that parsing a string whose tokens end right after a numeric token does not raise IndexError.

CONSTRAINTS: Make minimal changes; do NOT edit or delete any test file; do NOT break any currently passing test. Run `cd /dateutil && python -m pytest dateutil/test/ -q` before and after and ensure the failure set does not grow (report before/after). Also sanity-check `python -c "from dateutil.parser import parse; print(parse('Today is 25 of September of 2003, exactly at 10:49:41 with timezone -03:00.', fuzzy_with_tokens=True))"`.

REPORT: exactly which lines you changed, the new code, and pytest results before/after.
